findings.premise: Storing round content through the existing updateContent preserves earlier round outcomes in the log and satisfies ac12.
findings.evidence: DEF ac12 requires an entry 'with the round's outcome, so earlier rounds can still be read'. LifecycleService.updateContent supplies only `options: { operation: 'update' }`. ArtifactStore constructs entries with revision number/hash and includes outcome only when `options.outcome !== undefined`; it stores neither the old payload nor the new payload in the entry. The proposed three-argument RoundWriter cannot supply an outcome. Creating the first round without logging also leaves that round unavailable after its replacement. findings.premise: Current recovery can overwrite a moved head, and the current TESTS writer restores its prior JSON when markdown writing fails.
findings.evidence: completePending appends a missing entry, then executes `if (current !== op.bytes) ...writeHead...(path, op.bytes)` without checking the prior head. persistTestRecordTask captures priorJson, writes JSON before markdown, and restores priorJson or removes the new JSON in its markdown-failure catch. findings.action: Preserve the proposed recovery conflict check and the explicitly scoped rollback behavior.

Searches found no production durable implementations. ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion already accepts `{ writer: BuildContentWriter; actor: Actor }`, where updateContent takes id, actor and HeadPayload and returns Promise<boolean>. findings.premise: Existing heads without sidecars can pass lifecycle integrity checks with empty history.

findings.premise: An oversized entry rejected by appendRecord can be recovered simply by shortening the outcome and retrying.
findings.evidence: ArtifactStore calls `journal.stage` before `history.appendLog`. Subsequent writes and updates execute completePending first, which retries the immutable staged entry. summary.prose: s4 makes an artifact's change log and feedback durable and mergeable, and makes every production approval and review use the durable lifecycle service. Each head gets two append-only line files beside it (a Tasks file's files carry the lines of its Tasks); each line is length-framed so an abandoned fragment is told from corruption, and the files are marked merge=union in a committed .gitattributes, so two clones that add different entries merge without conflict while a changed head still conflicts in git. The write journal becomes a durable file that records the head a write started from, so recovery finishes a write but never overwrites a head that has moved on. The daemon keeps one store and one LifecycleService per repository and gives them to the approve handler, the review-decision step, the daemon review and the controller's verdicts phase, and the BUILD, TESTS and code-review records store their content through that service before their meta and markdown are refreshed, so each round is logged by the same staged write that replaces the record.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — lifecycle and sidecar storage

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

dataModelChanges.details: <id>.log.jsonl and <id>.feedback.jsonl beside the head in .insrc/artifacts. Each line is <byte length> TAB <SidecarRecord json> NEWLINE. The Tasks file's two files hold the lines of its Tasks. Lines are never rewritten or removed. Reader order is timestamp, then entry id; a repeated (artifactId, entry id) with the same content counts once.

dataModelChanges.entity: .gitattributes merge rules and the ignore entry
dataModelChanges.details: Two committed rules, '.insrc/artifacts/*.log.jsonl merge=union' and '.insrc/artifacts/*.feedback.jsonl merge=union', so git keeps the lines of both sides on merge. No rule is set for the head json, so a head changed in two clones conflicts and a person resolves it. The journal folder .insrc/journal/ is added to the ignore file. The store adds missing lines when it is created and never rewrites either file.
.insrc/journal/<id>.json holds one StagedOperation as JSON, replaced atomically, removed on clear. It is untracked because a staged write belongs to one working copy and must never be merged.
priorHeadHash: the sha-256 of the head bytes the write started from, absent for a create. Recovery replaces the head only when it still hashes to priorHeadHash or already equals the staged bytes.

{ writer: { updateContent(id, by, payload): Promise<boolean> }, actor: Actor }: what the round persisters take to store a record's content through the LifecycleService. It is the shape ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion already takes (s3), now shared by persistBuildRecord, persistTestRecordTask and CodeReviewRunnerDeps.

dataModelChanges.entity: Per-repository lifecycle registry in the daemon
dataModelChanges.details: One ArtifactStore (over the file sidecar and file journal, with the repository's clock), one History and one LifecycleService (createCompletionEvidence as its per-call evidence factory) per registered repository, created on first use and held by the daemon. The workflow.approve handler, the review-decision step, workflowReviewStart, the review-step handler's verdicts phase and the build and code-review step handlers take their service and RoundWriter from it. If creating it fails the request is refused with that error; there is no fallback to the head-only path inside the daemon.
through?: RoundWriter, used by runCodeReview before deps.write.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: s4 owns SidecarStorage: filesOf, appendRecord, readRecords and mergeAttributes as in the sketch, implemented over the s2 SidecarIo port. The line format is the SidecarRecord s2 defined, framed with its byte length; the file naming, the Tasks-file sharing, the union rules, the framing, the order and de-duplication are private to s4.

History is unchanged: it reads and appends through SidecarIo. s4 adds nothing to the entry shapes; a round's outcome uses the existing outcome field and the 'update' operation that ArtifactStore.update writes.
Implements the WriteJournal port and uses ArtifactStore.write and update as they are. The only change to the port's data is StagedOperation.priorHeadHash, which s2's follow-up 1 assigned to s4.

Wires LifecycleService over the durable store so approve, review and complete run the log-tail check on every production path (AMD-8), and uses its updateContent and inspect. Consumes checkIntegrity's reasons unchanged.
Parses ids with ArtifactIds.parse, and finds a Task's Tasks file by making the TASKS id from the Task's epic hash and Story.

errorCases.scenario: A crash tears the last line of a line file (the process dies mid-append), and a later append follows
errorCases.detection: appendRecord reads the last byte of the file before it writes and sees no newline; readRecords later finds a line whose frame is incomplete (no tab and length, or a length that does not match the json that follows)
errorCases.response: the append begins with a newline, so the fragment is a line of its own and the new record is a complete frame on the next line; the reader skips the fragment, logs it with the file and line, and still returns the later records, so torn text is never joined to a good record and never raises
errorCases.userImpact: none; the entry whose append was torn was not acknowledged, and its write is repaired from the journal when it had one

errorCases.scenario: A complete frame holds invalid json or is not a record (a hand edit, a bad merge)
errorCases.detection: readRecords reads a line whose byte length matches its frame and then fails to parse the json, or parses it to something other than an object with a string artifactId and an entry
errorCases.response: HistoryReadError naming the file and the line number; reads and writes of every artifact that shares that file are refused, approve included, because the log tail cannot be trusted
errorCases.userImpact: the artifact cannot be approved or completed until a person repairs the line; other files are unaffected

errorCases.scenario: A line file contains git merge markers because the union rule was missing when the branches merged
errorCases.detection: readRecords meets lines beginning with <<<<<<<, ======= or >>>>>>>, which are not complete frames
errorCases.response: they are skipped as fragments and logged as merge debris; both sides' complete frames stay in the file, so every entry is still read once and none is lost
errorCases.userImpact: the history reads correctly; the debris stays in the file until someone removes it, and the warning names the file

errorCases.scenario: Two frames carry the same artifact id and entry id with different content (an id collision or a hand edit)
errorCases.detection: readRecords compares a repeated (artifactId, entry id) with the first frame it kept
errorCases.response: identical content collapses silently; different content raises HistoryReadError naming both lines, because choosing one would hide an entry

errorCases.scenario: A staged write finds its head has moved on (writeArtifact or a merge changed the head after the stage)
errorCases.detection: completePending hashes the head and compares it with priorHeadHash and with the staged bytes; it matches neither
errorCases.response: LifecycleConflictError for that artifact, the journal file is kept, the three hashes are logged, and the entry is not appended a second time; nothing overwrites the head
errorCases.userImpact: the staged write does not complete and the artifact's writes and its approval are refused until a person compares the head with the staged bytes in .insrc/journal and resolves it or removes the journal file

errorCases.scenario: The journal file is present but is not a staged operation
errorCases.detection: WriteJournal.pending parses the file and checks operationId, priorRevision, bytes, entry and, when present, priorHeadHash
errorCases.response: an error naming the file; writes to that artifact are refused so nothing builds on an unknown state
errorCases.userImpact: that artifact cannot be written until the file is removed

errorCases.scenario: The process dies after the journal stage and before the log entry is appended
errorCases.detection: the next write, update or inspect finds a pending operation whose entry is not in the log
errorCases.response: completePending appends the staged entry, replaces the head when it still hashes to priorHeadHash, then clears

errorCases.scenario: The process dies after the log entry is appended and before the head is replaced (the log is ahead of the head)
errorCases.detection: the next write, update or inspect finds the pending operation with its entry already in the log and the head equal to priorHeadHash
errorCases.response: completePending replaces the head with the staged bytes and clears; the entry is not appended again, and LifecycleService.inspect finishes this before it reads, so approval never sees a spurious log-ahead-of-head

errorCases.scenario: The process dies after the head is replaced and before the journal is cleared
errorCases.detection: the pending operation's bytes equal the head

errorCases.scenario: A head holds merge conflict markers or is otherwise not a head after a merge
errorCases.detection: decodeArtifactHead raises ArtifactShapeError on the read
errorCases.response: the read fails with that error; the line files are untouched and nothing is merged automatically
errorCases.userImpact: a person resolves the head in git (ac13); reads of the artifact resume afterwards

errorCases.scenario: After a merge the union of both clones' log lines is ahead of, or disagrees with, the head that git kept
errorCases.detection: checkIntegrity in the LifecycleService on approve, review and complete reports log-ahead-of-head, head-ahead-of-log or hash-mismatch
errorCases.response: the operation is refused with LifecycleConflictError carrying the reason; nothing is written or logged
errorCases.userImpact: a person decides which side the head should follow; the conflict-resolved write adopts a head whose hash differs from its content

errorCases.scenario: A round's content cannot be stored when a BUILD, TESTS or CR record is replaced (the store refuses or the log append fails)
errorCases.detection: LifecycleService.updateContent throws inside persistBuildRecord, persistTestRecordTask or runCodeReview
errorCases.response: the persist fails with that error and writes nothing further: neither the record's meta nor its markdown, and the build verdict is returned with the error named instead of a quiet success; the staged write stays in the journal, and the next write, update or inspect of the artifact finishes it
errorCases.userImpact: the round is not recorded until the cause is fixed and the step is repeated; the earlier round and the log stay consistent, so approval and completion are not blocked by a half-recorded round

errorCases.scenario: The TESTS record's content is stored and then its markdown cannot be written
errorCases.detection: persistTestRecordTask catches the writeAtomic failure after updateContent resolved
errorCases.response: the content and its log entry stay committed and nothing is rolled back; the error is returned to the step, and the next persist of the record renders the markdown again
errorCases.userImpact: the markdown lags the record until the next persist; the log and the head agree

errorCases.scenario: The record to be replaced has no head yet (the first BUILD, TESTS or CR record of a Story)
errorCases.response: the persister creates the record with its raw writer and logs nothing, because there is no earlier round to keep; the next replacement goes through the store

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is asked to approve or review in a repository whose registry entry cannot be created
errorCases.detection: the registry builds the store and service on first use and the build throws (the artifacts folder cannot be read, the journal folder cannot be created)
errorCases.response: the request is refused with that error; the daemon does not fall back to the head-only path
errorCases.userImpact: the approval or review is not recorded half-way

errorCases.scenario: The .gitattributes rules or the ignore entry cannot be written (read-only checkout, permission)
errorCases.detection: the ensure step catches the write error when the store is created
errorCases.response: logged as a warning naming the missing lines and reported in the daemon's status; the store still works, but a merge of line files can leave markers until the rules are added
errorCases.userImpact: merge debris is skipped by the reader, so no entry is lost; the fix is to add the lines

errorCases.scenario: An entry is too large for one atomic append
errorCases.detection: appendRecord measures the serialised line against a cap of 256 KiB before it writes
errorCases.userImpact: the caller shortens the outcome data

errorCases.scenario: A step handler or writer that became async is still called without await
errorCases.detection: the typecheck fails on the Promise used as a value, and the write inventory test lists the changed writer files
errorCases.response: the call sites named in the contract are changed together; no unawaited call remains

edgeCases.input: Two clones each append different log entries to the same artifact, then merge
edgeCases.expected: git merges the log file with no conflict; a reader sees every entry once, ordered by timestamp then entry id

edgeCases.input: Two clones append the same entry (the same id and content), for example the same recovery run on a shared branch
edgeCases.expected: the union keeps both frames; the reader counts the entry once

edgeCases.input: A torn append, a later append, a re-read and a journal retry of the interrupted write in one sequence
edgeCases.expected: the fragment is skipped, the later record is read, and the retry appends its entry once, so the log holds the entry exactly once and reads without error

edgeCases.input: A Task's log entry is appended while its Tasks file has entries for other Tasks
edgeCases.expected: the frame goes to the Tasks file's log, and reading one Task returns only the frames whose artifactId is that Task

edgeCases.input: A TASK id whose Tasks head does not exist yet
edgeCases.expected: filesOf still returns the Tasks file's paths and an append creates them

edgeCases.input: A feedback entry and a log entry with the same timestamp
edgeCases.expected: openFeedback orders them by the shared (timestamp, id) rule, so the result does not depend on which file was read first

edgeCases.input: Feedback text containing newlines, tabs, quotes or a line separator character
edgeCases.expected: JSON.stringify escapes them, so the json is one line, and the frame's byte length counts the escaped text, so it reads back identical
the frame length is the byte length, not the character count, and the entry reads back identical

edgeCases.input: An artifact with no line files
edgeCases.expected: log and feedback are empty lists, logTail is undefined, and sc4 treats a log with no revision-bearing entry as no history

edgeCases.input: A repository that already has a .gitattributes or a .gitignore with other rules
edgeCases.expected: only the missing lines are appended, on their own lines, and nothing else changes

edgeCases.input: A round that changes nothing (the same content again)
edgeCases.expected: updateContent stores no revision and appends no entry, because an identical rewrite does not move the revision (k3)

invariantsToPreserve.text: A write stages its operation, appends its log entry, replaces the head atomically and then clears the journal, in that order, under the per-artifact queue; the order does not change when the journal becomes durable
Appending the same entry twice is harmless: a reader collapses a repeated (artifactId, entry id)
A change log or feedback line is never rewritten or removed once appended
appendSidecarLine stays the only function that writes a line file, so the write inventory keeps one raw append for history
A head with no log or feedback file behaves as before: it reads, writes and decodes with empty history
A recorded operation id is reused by a retry and never minted twice for one staged write
A record written without a RoundWriter (tests, tools with no daemon) is written exactly as before, including the TESTS json-then-markdown rollback

migration.stateBefore: SidecarIo and WriteJournal are ports with only in-memory implementations and one raw, unframed line append (src/workflow/artifact-core/sidecar.ts, src/workflow/artifact-core/journal.ts). History reads and appends through SidecarIo, and ArtifactStore writes stage in the journal, append the log entry and replace the head, but recovery replaces any head that differs from the staged bytes (src/workflow/artifact-core/store.ts). The repository has no .gitattributes and the daemon holds no ArtifactStore, History or LifecycleService, so approve and review run the head-only guard (src/workflow/gates.ts, src/daemon/index.ts, src/daemon/workflow-review-rpc.ts); the controller's verdicts phase writes with writeArtifact (src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/verdicts.ts). The BUILD, TESTS and CR records are replaced in place by synchronous writers (persistBuildRecord, persistTestRecordTask, runCodeReview's write dependency) with no log entry for the earlier round, and the TESTS writer rolls its json back when the markdown fails.
migration.stateAfter: The log and feedback of an artifact live in length-framed line files beside its head, union-merged by a committed .gitattributes and read filtered, de-duplicated and ordered; the journal is a durable untracked file that remembers the head a write started from, and recovery refuses to overwrite a head that moved on. The daemon holds one durable store, history and LifecycleService per repository, and the approve handler, the review-decision step, the daemon review and the verdicts phase all use them, so the full log-tail check runs on every path. The BUILD, TESTS and CR records store their content through the service before their meta and markdown are refreshed, so each round is logged by the staged write that replaces it, and a failed round log fails the persist instead of leaving the head ahead of its log.

migrationSteps.action: Add the framed line format to appendSidecarLine (with the torn-line guard and the size cap) and the file-backed SidecarIo and SidecarStore (filesOf, the filtered de-duplicated ordered read that skips fragments and merge debris, mergeAttributes) beside the in-memory one; nothing uses them yet.

Add priorHeadHash to StagedOperation, stage it in ArtifactStore.write, make completePending finish an operation only when the head is the prior head or already the staged bytes, and add the durable file journal. Run the existing recovery tests against both journals.
Give History.openFeedback the shared (timestamp, id) order, and make LifecycleService.inspect finish a staged write under the artifact's queue before it reads.
Add the ensure step that adds the two union merge rules to .gitattributes and the journal folder to the ignore file, adding only missing lines. Commit the two files for this repository.

Add the daemon's per-repository registry (store over the file sidecar and journal, history, LifecycleService with the per-call evidence factory) and pass it to the workflow.approve handler, the review-decision step and workflowReviewStart; the head-only path stays for callers with no daemon.

Make handleVerdicts async and give it the service; the review-step handler awaits it with the registry's service for the run's repository. The auto-fix goes through updateContent, the review stamp stays a meta-only write, and the review is applied on the lifecycle.

Make persistBuildRecord, persistStandaloneBuildRecord and persistTestRecordTask async with an optional RoundWriter, add through to the code-review runner dependencies, and change every caller (the validate and implement phases, ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion, the code-review step handler, the tests) to await them with the registry's RoundWriter. A failed content store fails the persist; a TESTS markdown failure after the content was stored is not rolled back.

Add the real-git two-clone merge tests, the framing and recovery matrix tests, the round-recording and failure tests, the wiring tests and the inventory entries; record the s9 inputs (existing artifacts have no line files, so the conversion back-fills history and writes the first entries).

migration.backwardCompat: No compatibility code. An artifact with no line files reads as an empty history, so every existing head keeps working. The in-memory SidecarIo and journal stay for tests only. The head-only gate path and the round writers' plain writeArtifact path (no RoundWriter) stay for callers that have no daemon (tests and tools), not as a fallback inside the daemon, which refuses a request when its registry entry cannot be created. Making persistBuildRecord, persistStandaloneBuildRecord, persistTestRecordTask and handleVerdicts async changes their signatures; all callers are in this repository and are changed together. Existing BUILD, TESTS and CR records gain log entries only from their next replacement; earlier rounds are not reconstructed (s9 back-fills what it can).

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-head framed line files, rounds through the store, one daemon registry
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Per-head log and feedback files with length-framed lines and union merge, a durable untracked journal, round records stored through LifecycleService.updateContent, and one per-repository registry the approval and review paths all take their service from.
alternativesConsidered.approach: FileSidecarStore implements SidecarIo and the sc5 SidecarStore. filesOf(id) returns { head: .insrc/artifacts/<id>.json, log: .insrc/artifacts/<id>.log.jsonl, feedback: .insrc/artifacts/<id>.feedback.jsonl }, with a TASK id mapped to the files of its Story's TASKS head. Each line is framed as <byte length> TAB <json> NEWLINE and written with one append-mode write; readRecords skips a frame whose length does not match (an abandoned fragment, logged), raises HistoryReadError for a complete frame whose json is invalid, keeps the lines of the requested artifact, collapses repeated (artifactId, entry id) and orders by timestamp then entry id. mergeAttributes() yields the two merge=union rules, ensured in .gitattributes with the journal folder in the ignore file. The journal is a file per artifact under .insrc/journal/<id>.json and StagedOperation gains priorHeadHash; completePending replaces a head only when it still has that hash or already equals the staged bytes. The content of a BUILD, TESTS or CR record is stored through LifecycleService.updateContent, awaited by the step handlers (validate, implement, the test-record caller, the code-review step handler, completion-record) before the synchronous raw writers refresh the record's meta and markdown; a failed store call fails that persist, and the staged write stays in the journal for the next write or update to finish. The daemon keeps one registry of {ArtifactStore, History, LifecycleService} per repository and gives it to the workflow.approve handler, the review-decision step, workflowReviewStart and the review step's verdicts phase.
pros: Round entries are committed by the same staged, queued write as every other change, so the log and the head cannot diverge and the earlier round stays readable
Framing separates an abandoned fragment from corruption even after later appends
One registry gives every approval and review path the same durable service, so the integrity check runs on all of them
Per-head files keep unrelated artifacts out of each other's merges and keep a log-tail read to one artifact
cons: Several step handlers and writers change from synchronous to awaited, and their callers with them
The raw meta and markdown writers still run after the store call, so a failure between the two leaves a re-runnable render, not a lost round
Two more files per head, and the ensure step is two more writers to inventory

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-head files with after-the-fact round events
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1 for layout and journal, but the round writers stay synchronous and a separate round event is appended to the log after they succeed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The layout, framing, journal and registry are as in a1. The BUILD, TESTS and CR writers keep replacing their record with writeArtifact, unchanged and synchronous; afterwards the step handler appends one log entry carrying the round's outcome and the record's new revision. A failed append is logged and surfaced in the step result, and the registry offers a repair call that appends the missing entry on the next approval.
pros: The synchronous writers and their callers do not change
A round is logged even though the record write is not staged
cons: Between the replace and the append the head is ahead of its log, the state the integrity check refuses, so a crash or a failed append blocks approval until the repair runs
The TESTS record's json-then-markdown rollback can leave a logged revision for content that was rolled back
Adds a repair call and a second way to write the log beside the staged write
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Keeps the writers synchronous but opens a window in which the head is ahead of its log and adds a second write path for the log.

alternativesConsidered.name: One repository-wide pair of framed line files
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Two framed line files for the whole repository, union-merged, with the rounds and the registry as in a1.
alternativesConsidered.approach: FileSidecarStore appends every record to .insrc/history/log.jsonl or .insrc/history/feedback.jsonl; readRecords scans the file for the artifact id. One attributes rule covers both files. Framing, journal, round recording and the registry are as in a1.
pros: Two files in total and one attributes rule
cons: Every clone appends to the same two files, so unrelated work overlaps at the file tail
A read scans the whole history for one artifact, which strains the load-time budget at about a thousand artifacts
A damaged frame in the shared file stops reads of every artifact
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Scan cost grows with the repository, unrelated artifacts share a merge tail, and one damaged frame blocks every artifact.

openQuestions: ep3: the invariants name the capability ids c1 to c4 whose citations point at the s1 bundles, but they do not quote the bundle text

After a merge the union of both clones' log lines can be ahead of the head git kept (log-ahead-of-head), and ArtifactStore.write refuses only a hash-mismatch: should a write on a log-ahead-of-head artifact also need the conflict-resolved option, or should the next ordinary write move the head up to the log?

The daemon's approval actor today is the gate itself (insrc:approval); the live tracker identity that k5 requires is s5's, so should s4 pass a person actor from the request when the client supplies one and fall back to the gate actor otherwise?

Making persistBuildRecord, persistStandaloneBuildRecord, persistTestRecordTask and handleVerdicts async touches many existing tests; should the tests be moved to the async forms in the same tasks as the writers, or kept on a thin synchronous test-only wrapper?
